item.content:encoded:
News / Cointelegraph / MSCI confirms Strategy’s removal from indexes at end of November

MSCI confirms Strategy’s removal from indexes at end of November Less than 1 min read

MSTR Index provider MSCI has confirmed Bitcoin treasury company Strategy will be removed from its global equity indexes, following months of debate over whether crypto treasury firms qualify as operating businesses. MSCI’s final list of affected securities, released as part of its November index review, lists “STRATEGY A” with the action “Deleted.” Japan’s Metaplanet and crypto treasury company Upexi are also marked for deletion, while Ether treasury firm Sharplink is on a watchlist. Strategy shares fell 1.65% in after-hours trading on Wednesday. The changes take effect after market close on Nov. 30, under the implementation timetable MSCI announced in October. Removal could prompt funds tracking the affected benchmarks to sell the companies’ shares, reducing a source of passive investment demand. As Cointelegraph reported in October, JPMorgan previously estimated that Strategy’s exclusion could trigger roughly $2.8 billion in selling. Strategy opposed the proposal, arguing that it repackaged MSCI’s earlier effort to exclude digital asset treasury companies and injected policy judgments into index construction. The company nevertheless played down the potential disruption. In its consultation response, Strategy said MSCI-linked funds held approximately 13 million shares, representing 3.1% of its basic shares outstanding and less than one day’s trading volume.

News / Seeking Alpha / Dollar Index crossed a 19-month high as the greenback continues to rally

Dollar Index crossed a 19-month high as the greenback continues to rally Less than 1 min read

DXY UUP USDU UDN The U.S. Dollar Index DXY climbed to 102.92 on Wednesday afternoon, advancing +0.7% and reaching its highest level in 19-months. The last time the DXY traded at this elevated range was April 10, 2025. The move unfolds on Veterans Day, when the bond market is closed, limiting activity in Treasuries and leaving currency markets as a primary focus. Despite the holiday backdrop, the greenback displayed firm underlying momentum. The index now sits above its 20-day, 50-day, 100-day, and 200-day moving averages, reinforcing a constructive technical picture. Year-to-date, the Dollar Index has gained +4.7% in 2026, reflecting a sustained period of strength for the currency. The combination of a fresh multi-month high and broad moving-average support underscores the dollar’s resilient tone even as domestic fixed-income markets remain shuttered. Traders will monitor whether the advance can be extended once full bond-market liquidity returns, with the current technical setup offering a clear reference point for near-term direction. U.S. Dollar Funds: UUP , USDU , and UDN . item.content:encoded:
News / Crypto Briefing / Square switches on Bitcoin payments by default for eligible US merchants

Square switches on Bitcoin payments by default for eligible US merchants 1 min read

XYZ BTCUSD Square has turned on Bitcoin payments by default for eligible US businesses. Sellers did not have to raise a hand, fill out a form, or sit through a webinar. The feature costs merchants 0% in processing fees through December 31. After that, a flat 1% fee kicks in. Square, the payments platform owned by Block, Inc., began auto-enabling Bitcoin acceptance on March 30, 2026. The full rollout across eligible sellers is scheduled to be complete by November 10, 2026. That reach matters. Square's merchant network includes over four million sellers. Payments run over the Lightning Network, a layer built on top of Bitcoin designed for fast, cheap transactions. The practical upshot is near-instant settlement. By default, merchants receive US dollars. The Bitcoin a customer sends is converted automatically at the moment of payment. Sellers who actually want to hold Bitcoin can choose to keep it instead. The fee schedule is straightforward. Processing is free through December 31, 2026, and moves to a flat 1% starting January 1, 2027. There are guardrails. Individual transactions are capped at approximately $600, and each seller faces a daily ceiling of about $20,000. Geography also limits the reach. The service is unavailable in New York and certain other jurisdictions. On the hardware side, Square says no new equipment is needed. The feature plugs into existing tools like Square Register and Invoices, along with Square's apps. Square is also letting businesses convert up to 50% of eligible daily card sales into Bitcoin. The move reflects Block's ongoing effort to embed crypto into everyday commerce. CEO Jack Dorsey and Bitcoin product head Miles Suter are steering the initiative. The pitch tackles two complaints small businesses tend to have about accepting Bitcoin: volatility and operational hassle. Automatic dollar conversion addresses the first. Integration with existing Square tools addresses the second. Shifting from opt-in to on-by-default is the bigger philosophical change. For merchants, the near-term calculus is simple. Through December 31, accepting Bitcoin costs nothing in processing fees, requires no new hardware, and pays out in dollars unless the seller says otherwise. The approximately $600 transaction cap and roughly $20,000 daily ceiling limit high-value use cases, and the exclusion of New York and other jurisdictions shows regulation still shapes where this can operate.
